protected_setup.thesis: NVIDIA has gone from a leadership shock to a valuation floor in nine sessions: 239.24 on 6 Oct to 125.53 on 20 Nov (-47.5%), then +31.5% on 23 Nov when the board re-hired Jensen Huang, then -5.9% on 24 Nov to 155.38, and 146.04 in the 25 Nov premarket while the whole AI complex is down 3-5% on a reported tariff threat to 16 trading partners and a core PCE print of 3.3% y/y, the highest since Nov 2023. It buys only if the price reclaims the 24 Nov low of 150.50 and trades back into 151-156, which is the level the 24 Nov close left and the level the bounce has to hold for the 23 Nov reversal to mean anything. Fundamentally the stock trades near 10x forward earnings, its cheapest multiple since 2008 and the lowest of the Mag-7, after at least three sell-side upgrades since the re-hire with targets of 220 (Goldman), 220 (UBS), 240 (Citi) and 270 (StoneX); the mean target implies about +57% over twelve months.
